recipes.name: Sausage Stuffed Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package Johnsonville® Ground Italian Sausage

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Line baking sheets with aluminum foil.
Crumble and cook sausage in a skillet over medium heat until no longer pink and lightly browned; drain.
Remove and discard mushroom stems; arrange caps on the prepared baking sheets.
Combine cooked sausage, cream cheese, bread crumbs, parsley, garlic, and lemon juice in a bowl; stir until blended. Spoon sausage mixture into mushroom caps; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until mushrooms are tender and lightly browned, 14 to 16 minutes.

review.reviewBody: These are good, but the filling is even better the next day! I'd suggest making it in advance, then fill your mushrooms when you're ready to bake them. I used baby portabello mushrooms. *I made these again as written but left the breadcrumbs out to stay with a low carb diet--they turned out perfectly and are delicious!!

I love the flavor and ease of this recipe, but I did add a couple of my own touches. I halved the recipe and added the stems and half an onion, which I blitzed in the food processor and added to the sausage when it was half way cooked. Once it was fully cooked, I added the garlic for a minute. Then I added the sausage/stem/onion mixture back to the food processor to get smaller crumbles. Made the stuffing hold together really well and it is a big hit with my husband. I added the grated cheese directly to the stuffing mix and I did omit the lemon due to my husband's preference. I put them under the broiler for 1.5 minutes after they were cooked through.

I was hosting out of town guests and they commented that they loved mushrooms. When I came across this recipe, I decided to give it a try. However, I used large portobello mushrooms and served it as an entree for dinner one evening. Other than sauteing my garlic before adding to the mixture, I followed the recipe exactly. However, I tasted the stuffing before filling the mushrooms and determined it was a bit bland, as other reviews stated. I added a pinch of salt and black pepper. The game changer in flavor was the addition of onion. I only had onion powder on hand so I added that to taste. The addition of onion took this recipe from 4 stars to 5 stars. I chopped the mushroom stems, sauteed them and added them to the mixture as well. My guests raved over the meal, even stating they thought it was so much better than the highly rated, award winning BBQ restaurant I took them to for lunch. They even asked for the recipe before they left. I cannot eat mushrooms so I cannot comment on the taste of the finished product. However, I was extremely pleased the recipe was such a huge hit! I also love that this recipe is SUPER easy, quick to make, and easy to adapt for personal preference!

Used hot Italian sausage, onions with a pinch of baking soda and 2 cloves of garlic, added asiago cheese to the mix and a little bit of panko breadcrumbs, touch of lemon juice and 8 oz of cream cheese. I chopped and sautéed the stems and added to the sausage mixture. I used large portabella mushrooms and sprinkled grated asiago cheese on top and baked for 15 minutes. Absolutely delicious, rave reviews!

My boyfriend loves these and practically begs me to make them. I don't discard the stems, I chop them up and put them in the sausage mixture while cooking. They disappear really fast and other than using the stem, I follow the recipe exactly the way it calls for.

Easy recipe and everyone raved about them! It was my first time eating let alone making stuffed mushrooms. I added some green bell pepper and onion while cooking the sausage. Will definitely be making again!
After preparing the mushrooms, I baked them in the pan on a bar-be-que pit over mesquite coals. The smokiness added a wonderful flavor and my guests were over the moon with the appetizers!!

I made this appy recipe as a entree for dinner by using large portabella mushrooms and we loved it! I doubled the minced garlic as usual with any recipe I make. I also used freshly grated peccorino romano as we prefer the rich taste over parmesan. Thank you, Johnsonville!

I will make these again but with small differences. These are easy to make and I really loved the idea of this. Since my family loves garlic I kind of went overboard on that part and that was the predominant taste. So next time I will go a bit lighter on the garlic! I used turkey hot Italian sausage as pork is so fatty and it didn’t bother me to change that up because it was still Italian suausage. I forgot about the bread crumbs and didn’t have any on hand so I omitted that, which I think is just fine. I honestly don’t think the little bit of bread crumbs asked would have made that much of a difference. I also didn’t have fresh parsley so I had to use dried parsley flakes. I bought huge white mushrooms so the filling only filled up 13 instead of 24, which was fine with me because there were only 4 of us eating them. Oh! I chopped up the stems and added them to the mixture, per some other reviews.The verdict: everyone agreed the garlic was too much but otherwise liked them. My husband generally isn’t overly crazy about mushrooms but thought these were “quite tasty”. For myself, I thought them to be bland. I will definitely use fresh parsley next time and maybe add another fresh herb to it. It just needs to be spiced up a bit. The sausage didn’t have much of a taste, which surprised me because we always use turkey Italian sausage and think it tastes great. There’s definitely many things that could be added to this to change up the flavor depending on one’s taste.

I think this recipe was a bit bland. It needs a bit of salt and maybe some pepper too. As others suggested, I chopped the stalks and cooked them with the Italian sausage. I will think about it to make them next time, but if I do, I will add the aforementioned ingredients and probably a bit more garlic or think of something else.

I love these- just like gigi used to make! I used spicy sausage, omitted the parsley and used parmesan-reggiano cheese. I ended up having extra so I added the stuffing mixture to baby bell peppers, the small sweet ones and I loved the combination of flavors.
I deep fried them and had to make a nother batch.

We loved this. I used 1.5 oz of mild Italian sausage but I wished I used hot. I added more parm cheese to the recipe and on the top. Also added the mushroom stems to make it less rich. Made 1/2 last night and 2nd half tonight. I didn't use bread crumbs just because I didn't see the need for them.
LOVED THESE!!
These turned out great. I chose not to use the lemon juice and I chopped up my mushroom stems and cooked them with the sausage. I also used dried parsley instead of fresh.
It was easy and delicious. I also chopped up the stems and used them too
Everyone loved them. Gone in minutes!
I used less than the 1/2 cup of breadcrumbs because the texture started to get dry. Also used dried parsley because I didn't have fresh. It turned out delicious!
Easy to assemble. Added celery and jalopenos
These were a hit at New Year's Eve! I added breadcrumbs to the top and they got nice and browned/crunchy
